newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue strong despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue strong despite strike.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares marched to new highs in an active market on Thursday despite the government's ongoing pay dispute with striking civil servants.
The key industrial index surged 39.93 points -- or 0.7 percent -- to an all-time high of 5,758.09.
"The ongoing wrangles had no effect on the market. It is very firm," one broker said.

Zimbabwe's civil servants carried their strike into its ninth day despite a government announcement on Thursday that it was awarding them a 20 percent wage increase in addition to an up to nine percent award it made recently which they rejected.

The government did not, however, clarify whether it would reverse its decision to fire the strikers -- estimated by the Public Service Association at between 70 and 80 percent of the country's 180,000 public servants.
The strikers -- including doctors, nurses, mortuary attendants and firefighters -- said they would stay on the streets until the government settled the issue of the dismissals.
Brokers said it was too early to say what effect the government's wage increases would have on the market as it was not clear how it would finance them.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Thursday, publishing group Zimpapers soared 415 cents to 1,025 on the back of an announcement earlier in the day of a boost in share earnings and dividend for the half-year ended June 30.

Bankers FMB and pottery-maker Ariston jumped 100 cents each to 2,900 and 1,000 respectively, Rothmans at 2,450 and investment house Northchart at 1,100 both rose 50 cents while conglomerate TA Holdings gained 30 cents to 150 and steel firm FSI was 20 cents up to 220.
Tyre manufacturer Dunlop was the sole loser, slipping five cents to 155.
In minings, Falgold and copper counter Mhangura traded at previous levels while Wankie Colliery added five cents to 315 and gold producer Falcon rose 50 cents to 1,600.
The mining index edged a marginal 0.76 points to 1,277.77.
